**File:** `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`
**Detected topic:** Cloudron App Platform Guide
**Current size:** 262 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### CRITICAL: coderabbit (coderabbitai[bot])
**File**: `.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md:564`
**Verification**: kept as unverifiable (no stable snippet extracted)
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Follow-up triage logic is broken because maintainer comment timestamp is never populated.**

Line 572 reads `.created_at` from `COMMENT_DATA`, but the documented `COMMENT_DATA` projection only includes `body` and `id`. This makes the recency comparison unreliable and can prevent intended follow-up triage dispatches.



<details>
<summary>Proposed doc fix</summary>

```diff
-COMMENT_DATA=$(gh api "repos/<slug>/issues/<number>/comments" \
-  --jq "[.[] | select(.user.login == \"$MAINTAINER\")] | last | {body: .body, id: .id}")
+COMMENT_DATA=$(gh api "repos/<slug>/issues/<number>/comments" \
+  --jq "[.[] | select(.user.login == \"$MAINTAINER\")] | last | {body: .body, id: .id, created_at: .created_at}")
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md around lines 566 - 573, The maintainer
recency check fails because MAINTAINER_COMMENT_DATE extracts .created_at from
COMMENT_DATA even though COMMENT_DATA projection only includes body and id;
update the COMMENT_DATA projection to include created_at (or the correct
timestamp field) so MAINTAINER_COMMENT_DATE=$(echo "$COMMENT_DATA" | jq -r
'.created_at // empty') returns a value, and ensure the script refers to the
same field name consistently when computing LAST_REVIEW_DATE and comparing
timestamps (references: COMMENT_DATA, MAINTAINER_COMMENT_DATE,
LAST_REVIEW_DATE).
```

</details>

title: feature: Adopt skills from audn-ai/penclaw repository
body:
## Proposal

Adopt relevant skills from the [audn-ai/penclaw](https://github.com/audn-ai/penclaw) repository. Penclaw is an OpenClaw-compatible skill marketplace with 51 skills covering productivity, DevOps, and AI tooling.

## Skills Available

The penclaw repo contains 51 skills across categories:

### Productivity & Notes
1password, apple-notes, apple-reminders, bear-notes, notion, obsidian, things-mac, trello

### Communication
discord, himalaya, imsg, slack, eightctl

### Media & Entertainment
blucli, bluebubbles, camsnap, gog, songsee, sonoscli, spotify-player, video-frames

### DevOps & CLI Tools
blogwatcher, clawhub, github, goplaces, mcporter, openai-whisper, openai-whisper-api, peekaboo, sag, session-logs, tmux, wacli, xurl

### AI & Development
coding-agent, gemini, model-usage, skill-creator, summarize, supermemory

### Infrastructure
nano-pdf, node-connect, openhue, oracle, ordercli, healthcheck, himalaya, sherpa-onnx-tts, weather

### GitHub Integration
gh-issues, github

## Recommendation

Prioritize high-value skills not currently in aidevops:

1. **1password** — 1Password CLI integration (vs current gopass)
2. **coding-agent** — Multi-agent orchestration (codex, claude, pi, opencode)
3. **peekaboo** — Browser automation (may complement existing)
4. **mcporter** — MCP server management (useful for MCP tooling)
5. **obsidian** — Obsidian vault integration
6. **summarize** — Content summarization
7. **session-logs** — Session logging (relates to #11498)

## Approach

1. Fork or track penclaw as upstream via skill-sources.json
2. Ingest priority skills following existing conventions (see shannon.md pattern)
3. Register in subagent-index.toon and domain-index.md

## Reference

- Penclaw skills: https://github.com/audn-ai/penclaw/tree/main/skills
- Existing aidevops skill structure: .agents/tools/security/shannon.md

title: t1695: FOSS contribution pipeline — core orchestrator + handler framework
body:
## Summary

Create `foss-contribution-helper.sh` — the orchestration layer for contributing PRs to open-source repos we use. Scans open issues on registered FOSS repos, triages for fixability, forks, creates worktrees, delegates build/test to app_type-specific handlers, and submits PRs upstream.

## Motivation

We have idle machine time and spare daily token budget. Contributing fixes to FOSS projects we depend on (WordPress plugins, Nextcloud, EspoCRM, macOS apps, CLI tools, etc.) is high-leverage: we improve our own stack while giving back. The framework already has external repo submission rules (t1407), contribution watch (t1419), headless dispatch, and localdev infrastructure — but no automated "find issue → fix → test → PR" pipeline.

## Scope

- `foss-contribution-helper.sh` with subcommands: `add-repo`, `scan`, `triage`, `contribute`, `status`
- Handler interface: each `app_type` implements `setup`, `build`, `test`, `review`, `cleanup`
- Handler directory: `.agents/scripts/foss-handlers/`
- Integration with existing: `external-repo-submissions.md` (template compliance), `contribution-watch-helper.sh` (follow-up monitoring), `headless-runtime-helper.sh` (dispatch), `localdev-helper.sh` (HTTPS review URLs for HTTP-serving apps)
- Etiquette controls: max PRs per repo per period, disclosure line in PR descriptions, blocklist support
- Pulse integration: runs on idle capacity only, respects token budget ceiling

## Subtasks

- [ ] t1696: WordPress plugin handler (wp-env + multisite + localdev)
- [ ] t1697: repos.json schema extension + budget controls
- [ ] t1698: Generic handler + app_type detection

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `foss-contribution-helper.sh scan` lists actionable issues from registered FOSS repos
- [ ] `foss-contribution-helper.sh contribute <slug> <issue>` forks, clones, creates worktree, delegates to handler, submits PR
- [ ] Handler interface documented with at least 2 implementations (wordpress-plugin + generic)
- [ ] Etiquette controls enforced (rate limiting, disclosure, blocklist)
- [ ] Integration tests pass

title: t1697: FOSS contribution — repos.json schema extension + budget controls
body:
## Summary

Extend repos.json schema to support FOSS contribution targets with app_type classification and budget/etiquette controls.

## Parent

t1695 (#12251)

## Scope

- New repos.json fields: `foss: true`, `app_type` (enum), `foss_config` object
- `app_type` values: `wordpress-plugin`, `php-composer`, `node`, `python`, `go`, `macos-app`, `browser-extension`, `cli-tool`, `electron`, `cloudron-package`, `generic`
- `foss_config` object: `max_prs_per_week` (default 2), `token_budget_per_issue` (max tokens per contribution attempt), `blocklist` (boolean, maintainer asked us to stop), `disclosure` (boolean, include AI assistance note in PRs, default true), `labels_filter` (array of labels to scan for, e.g. ["help wanted", "bug", "needs-patch"])
- Global budget config in `~/.config/aidevops/config.jsonc`: `foss.enabled`, `foss.max_daily_tokens`, `foss.max_concurrent_contributions`

- Schema documentation in `reference/planning-detail.md` or new `reference/foss-contributions.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] repos.json accepts `foss: true` + `app_type` + `foss_config` without breaking existing tooling
- [ ] `foss-contribution-helper.sh scan` respects `labels_filter` and skips `blocklist: true` repos
- [ ] Budget ceiling enforced: contributions refused when daily token limit reached
- [ ] Schema documented with examples for each app_type

title: t1698: FOSS contribution — generic handler + app_type detection
body:
## Summary

Create the generic/fallback handler and app_type auto-detection logic for the FOSS contribution pipeline. The generic handler reads the repo's README/CONTRIBUTING.md to determine build/test commands. Auto-detection infers app_type from repo contents when not explicitly set in repos.json.

## Parent

t1695 (#12251)

## Scope

### Generic handler (`foss-handlers/generic.sh`)
- `setup`: clone, read README + CONTRIBUTING.md, detect package manager (package.json → npm, composer.json → composer, Makefile → make, Cargo.toml → cargo, go.mod → go, setup.py/pyproject.toml → pip/poetry, *.xcodeproj → xcodebuild)
- `build`: run detected build command
- `test`: run detected test command, report pass/fail
- `review`: if HTTP-serving, wire to localdev; if native app, report build artifact path; if CLI, report binary path
- `cleanup`: stop processes, remove localdev registration if applicable

### App_type auto-detection (`detect-app-type.sh` or function in orchestrator)
- Scan repo root for marker files → infer app_type
- Marker map: `style.css` with `Plugin Name:` header → `wordpress-plugin`, `composer.json` → `php-composer`, `package.json` → `node`, `*.xcodeproj` or `Package.swift` → `macos-app`, `manifest.json` with `browser_action` → `browser-extension`, `CloudronManifest.json` → `cloudron-package`, `go.mod` → `go`, `Cargo.toml` → `rust`, `pyproject.toml`/`setup.py` → `python`
- Falls back to `generic` if no markers match
- Result cached in repos.json on first detection

### macOS app handler stub (`foss-handlers/macos-app.sh`)
- `setup`: clone, detect Xcode project vs Swift Package
- `build`: `xcodebuild` or `swift build`
- `test`: `xcodebuild test` or `swift test`
- `review`: open built .app or report binary path
- No localdev URL (native app)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Auto-detection correctly identifies app_type for: a WordPress plugin, a Node project, a Go project, a macOS app, a Cloudron package
- [ ] Generic handler successfully builds and tests a simple Node project and a simple Go project
- [ ] macOS app handler builds and runs tests for a Swift Package project
- [ ] Handler gracefully fails with clear error when build/test commands can't be determined
- [ ] Detected app_type written back to repos.json for future runs

title: Bug: list_active_worker_processes misses /bin/.opencode workers (dispatched via headless-runtime-helper)
body:
## Observed

`list_active_worker_processes` in `pulse-wrapper.sh` filters out processes matching `/\/bin\/\.opencode[[:space:]]/` (line: `$0 !~ /\/bin\/\.opencode[[:space:]]/`). However, workers dispatched by `headless-runtime-helper.sh` on this system run as `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/.opencode` — which matches this exclusion pattern.

## Impact

The pulse reports 0 active workers when there are actually 15+ running. This causes:
1. Over-dispatch (pulse fills all 24 slots when they're already occupied)
2. Stale worker (PID 33773) running for 1h11m on a closed issue (#12282) was not detected
3. Worker count used for capacity planning is always 0, making MAX_WORKERS enforcement ineffective

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The exclusion pattern was intended to filter out the opencode TUI/interactive process (not workers), but it's too broad — it matches the full path `/bin/.opencode` anywhere in the command string, including worker processes.

## Proposed Fix

The exclusion should only filter the opencode TUI (interactive session), not worker processes. Workers can be identified by the presence of `/full-loop` or `/review-issue-pr` in their command args. title: Bug: model-availability-helper.sh resolve returns stale opencode model IDs (gemini-3-pro vs gemini-3.1-pro)
body:
Observed: `model-availability-helper.sh resolve opus` returned `opencode/gemini-3-pro` but the correct model ID is `opencode/gemini-3.1-pro`. Workers launched with the wrong ID fail immediately with ProviderModelNotFoundError suggesting `gemini-3.1-pro`. Root cause hypothesis: The opencode model cache in model-availability-helper is hardcoded or stale and doesn't reflect the actual model IDs returned by `opencode models`. Proposed fix: The helper should query `opencode models` to validate model IDs before returning them, or the hardcoded fallback chain should use the correct versioned IDs. Impact: All workers dispatched with the wrong model ID fail at startup, wasting dispatch slots and issue comments.

title: [Caret^] Integration: 28-62% doc reduction, behavioral parity gaps, adoption notes
body:
## Care t^ Integration — Findings Report

Integrated Caret^ notation from `disruptionjoe/caret` into aidevops. Formal analysis via 5-lens Caret-it methodology.

### What Was Done
1. Fetched and analyzed full Caret^ repo from `disruptionjoe/caret`
2. Created `skills/caret.md` — aidevops framework integration skill with scalars, directives, pattern mappings
3. Created `skills/caret-cheatsheet.md` — canonical cheatsheet from upstream
4. Created `workflows/git-workflow-careted.md` — full Caret^ conversion of git-workflow (197→207 lines, 28% reduction)
5. Created `workflows/pre-edit-careted.md` — before/after comparison for pre-edit workflow (118→42 lines, 62% reduction)
6. Fixed nesting bug: `^^^^lifecycle-pipeline` → `^^lifecycle-pipeline` (was depth 5, should be depth 3)

### Reduction Results

| File | Original | Caret | Reduction |
|------|----------|--------|-----------|
| `pre-edit.md` | 3,609 bytes | ~1,600 bytes | ~56% |
| `git-workflow.md` | 7,969 bytes | 5,744 bytes | 28% |

Note: git-workflow resists high compression because it is heavy on lookup tables and code blocks.

### Caret-it Formal Analysis (git-workflow-careted.md)

**Verdict: HYBRID — PARTIAL behavioral parity**

| Lens | Finding |
|------|---------|
| **Scope fidelity** | PARTIAL — `^^^^lifecycle-pipeline` nesting bug; lifecycle-pipeline at depth 5 instead of 3 |
| **Safety parity** | PARTIAL — `--force-with-lease` missing from blocked commands list |
| **Resolution completeness** | PARTIAL — `session-rename_sync_branch` reference dropped |
| **Concreteness resolution** | PASS — all directives resolved to specific files/commands |
| **Action mapping** | PASS — code actions mapped, planning actions preserved |

### Known Behavioral Gaps
1. **Nesting bug fixed** — `^^^^lifecycle-pipeline` → `^^lifecycle-pipeline`
2. **`--force-with-lease` missing** from blocked commands list in careted version
3. **`session-rename_sync_branch` dropped** — was a non-standard directive, unclear if needed

### Files Ready for PR

```
.agents/skills/caret.md                          # skill (updated with adoption notes)
.agents/skills/caret-cheatsheet.md              # canonical cheatsheet
.agents/workflows/git-workflow-careted.md         # careted git-workflow (nesting bug fixed)
.agents/workflows/pre-edit-careted.md             # before/after comparison
```

### Next Steps
- [ ] Open PR to aidevops
- [ ] Consider `caret-extensions.md` for framework-specific directives
- [ ] Add formal before/after validation to CI

---

*Generated from steganography analysis session. Caret^ integration skill is at `skills/caret.md`.*
